talking_points.headline: OpenAI cuts off Musk's Cursor; Anthropic doubles down — a live vendor lock-in case study
talking_points.context_html: OpenAI will end model access for Cursor on 12 November after Elon Musk's SpaceX bought the $60bn coding platform, citing distrust in how Musk's companies have handled past agreements; Anthropic co-founder Tom Brown responded by promising more Claude compute to keep the tool running smoothly. The episode shows AI labs increasingly picking sides based on who owns the distribution channel, not just model quality — a dynamic worth weighing before committing further agentic-coding or change-execution workflows to any single AI vendor.

AI & Technology.title: OpenAI to cut Cursor's model access after Musk's SpaceX buys it; Anthropic boosts Claude compute
AI & Technology.summary: OpenAI said it will end Cursor's access to its models on 12 November, citing distrust in how Elon Musk's companies honour contracts after SpaceX's $60bn acquisition of the coding platform; Anthropic co-founder Tom Brown immediately pledged more Claude compute to keep serving Cursor instead. It is a fresh flashpoint in the AI vendor-concentration story tracked in recent briefings (Anthropic's Nscale compute deal, its IPO run-up), showing model providers now compete on distribution loyalty as much as raw capability. For a bank standardising change-execution or engineering workflows on a single foundation-model provider, it is a live illustration of the lock-in risk that needs underwriting before scaling agentic coding tools further.

Regulatory & Markets.title: US strikes on Iranian forces near Strait of Hormuz send oil sharply higher, rate-hike odds climb
Regulatory & Markets.summary: The US military struck Iranian rocket launchers near the Strait of Hormuz on Sunday, reigniting a conflict that has repeatedly disrupted the strait since February and pushing global benchmark crude up 2% at the Asia open. It lands on top of Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's hawkish Jackson Hole remarks, which had already pushed September rate-hike odds above 55%, compounding market uncertainty into the new week. For Adam, a renewed oil shock stacked on higher-for-longer US rate expectations raises near-term volatility for HNW client portfolios and adds to the funding-cost pressure already weighing on Asia private-banking margins.
